title: Design notes for a job queue
persona: You are a candidate submitting a take-home project.
context: Project facts: Background job queue in Node.js on top of Postgres. Workers use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so several workers can pull jobs without taking the same one. Failed jobs retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff, then move to a dead-letter table. A job can run more than once if a worker crashes after finishing it but before marking it done, so handlers must be idempotent. You picked Postgres over Redis to avoid running another service. Throughput topped out near 800 jobs per second with 4 workers in your benchmark.
